flagship.name: Main Street Radar — Search Readiness OS
why: Extends the working provenance and scoring product instead of creating a second system.
Demonstrates product, data, workflow, and AI-safety judgment with credential-free fixtures.
Can support a client-controlled preparation sprint without claiming brokerage, advice, financing, or outreach.

recommendedPath.label: Self-funded-size preparation lane
recommendedPath.boundary: A reversible 12-week preparation lane, not a financing application, eligibility claim, capital commitment, or acquisition path selection.

strategyHypothesis.geography: United States; exact regions are a Miles-owned decision
requiredCharacteristics: Repeat, recurring, or contracted demand that can be verified
Retention and concentration disclosed before advance
A credible owner transition and trainable operating model
Positive cash generation after market manager cost and reinvestment
exclusions: No conversion between SDE and EBITDA labels
No lead advances with unknown current availability presented as active
Avoid customer concentration, owner dependence, or licensing risk until evidenced
No financing, seller note, or SBA eligibility assumed from a listing
No regulated or safety-critical vertical without qualified diligence capacity

decisionInputs.label: SDE or EBITDA basis and range
Debt, guarantee, concentration, and loss limits

paths.label: Traditional search fund
paths.evidenceMaturity: High for core-model history; unknown for Miles-specific access, terms, and outcome
dependencies: Full-time commitment and private runway decision
Comfort with investor governance, dilution, and vesting
Qualified securities, legal, tax, and accounting review
paths.continueCriteria: Continue only after full-time commitment, protected private runway, governance acceptance, and a professionally reviewed communication path.
paths.stopCriteria: Stop or pause if full-time search or investor governance is unacceptable, preparation consumes the protected reserve, or professional review rejects the proposed structure.

paths.label: Self-funded / SBA-style
paths.evidenceMaturity: High for SBA program boundaries; unknown for Miles-specific eligibility, terms, and capacity
dependencies: Private runway, liquidity floor, and maximum concentration decision
Tolerance for debt, guarantees, collateral, and owner-operator duties
Target-specific cash-flow evidence and lender pre-screen
Qualified legal, tax, accounting, and lending review
paths.continueCriteria: Continue only if private risk limits fit the target size and a real target later passes lender and professional review.
paths.stopCriteria: Stop or reduce target size if required buyer capital breaches the protected liquidity limit or indicated debt fails downside coverage.

paths.label: Independent sponsor
paths.evidenceMaturity: Descriptive practitioner evidence; unknown for Miles-specific credibility, capital relationships, and terms
dependencies: Broken-deal loss limit and sponsor co-invest decision
Qualified securities, broker-dealer, legal, tax, and accounting review
paths.continueCriteria: Continue only with a credible target thesis, evidenced execution fit, tolerable broken-deal exposure, and a plausible but uncommitted capital-provider universe.
paths.stopCriteria: Stop if the path depends on unearned credibility, capital appearing only after exclusivity, or compensation and governance that cannot pass professional review.

roadmap.acceptance: Exact chats and repo state linked; summaries are not treated as authority.
Required thesis, runway, time, and risk fields are decided or explicitly deferred.
Three paths compared with personal inputs still private and unknown by default.
Schemas and fixtures validate with no connector, account, or external mutation.
Every retained lead has canonical provenance; blocked and conflicting fetches stay visible.
screen-v1.0 limits are documented and deterministic regression checks pass.
Coverage gaps lead; KPI denominators and decision queue are explicit.
Privacy-safe pointers and review states work; no gated documents enter git.
Unknown inputs cannot produce a balanced case, DSCR, approval, or eligibility label.
Synthetic drafts remain unsent with sentAt null and no send path.
Employer demo passes and target-user feedback is recorded separately from demand claims.
A decision memo records evidence, risks, dependencies, and any later approval gate.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Exact prior chats and live repository state
Path comparison plus private runway, time, and risk decisions
decisionGates.passResult: One preparation path is selected; no capital claim.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Model reconciliation, version decision, and passing checks
decisionGates.passResult: Screen may be used beyond the demo within its stated boundary.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Exact recipient, channel, template, suppression, claim, and approval record
decisionGates.passResult: A later narrowly approved outbound action; no seller interest implied.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Scorecard, risks, requested evidence, and conflicts
decisionGates.passResult: Advance, hold, or decline a target.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Exact audience, materials, path, and current legal review
decisionGates.passResult: A later permitted communication scope only.

decisionGates.requiredEvidence: Target-specific diligence, financing, structure, and approvals
decisionGates.passResult: A separate commitment decision outside pre-launch scope.

risks.statement: Personal decisions are replaced by favorable defaults.
risks.mitigation: Keep user-owned fields unknown until G1 and G2 are explicitly decided.

risks.statement: A stale or blocked listing is presented as currently available.
risks.mitigation: Preserve retrieval date, availability claim, and coverage gaps; refresh before action.

risks.statement: Multiple engines are mistaken for independent corroboration of one source.
risks.mitigation: Track canonical lineage and retain conflicts without overwriting.

risks.statement: A score is treated as valuation, underwriting approval, or buy recommendation.
risks.mitigation: Show fixed rubric, caps, evidence states, and human decision gates everywhere.

risks.statement: Illustrative capital math is treated as financing availability or eligibility.
risks.mitigation: Label all scenarios illustrative and withhold outputs when target inputs are unknown.

risks.statement: Sensitive client, tax, bank, or gated diligence data enters source control.
risks.mitigation: Store only privacy-safe metadata pointers and hashes; keep raw material outside git.

risks.statement: Draft outreach is mistaken for approval, send, or seller engagement.
risks.mitigation: Keep drafts synthetic, draftOnly true, sentAt null, and provide no send control.

risks.statement: Consulting compensation or activity crosses legal, securities, or broker-dealer boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Exclude transaction intermediation and success-compensation recommendations pending qualified counsel.

risks.statement: Tool polish is presented as target-user validation or business demand.
risks.mitigation: Separate automated checks, usability evidence, willingness to pay, clients, and revenue claims.

risks.statement: The weekly workflow exceeds approved capacity and becomes noisy inventory work.
risks.mitigation: Time-box the cadence, suppress unchanged leads, and pause after two capacity overruns.

outreachTemplates.subject: Question about {{listingTitle}}
outreachTemplates.body: Hi {{firstName}}, I am reviewing {{listingTitle}} for fit with a documented acquisition thesis. Before deciding whether to request further information, could you confirm current availability and the source label and period for the reported earnings? I have not assumed SBA eligibility, seller financing, or accuracy of the listing figures. Thank you, {{senderName}}

outreachTemplates.subject: Private, exploratory conversation about {{companyName}}
outreachTemplates.body: Hi {{firstName}}, I am researching companies in {{industry}} and came across {{companyName}} through public information. I do not know whether you are considering a transaction. If a confidential introductory conversation would ever be useful, I can share the scope and participants for review first. No action has been taken from this draft. Best, {{senderName}}

outreachTemplates.subject: Following up: {{topic}}
outreachTemplates.body: Hi {{firstName}}, one brief follow-up on my note about {{topic}}. If this is not relevant, no response is needed and I will close the item. If it is relevant, please suggest the appropriate next step. Thank you, {{senderName}}
